newsitem.title: ITALY: Emporio Armani tones muted, Missoni loud and clear.
newsitem.headline: Emporio Armani tones muted, Missoni loud and clear.

text.p: Subtle fabric contrasts and dusky colours characterised Italian designer Giorgio Armani's Emporio Armani women's collection for the autumn/winter 1997/98 season.

Armani, showing the ready-to-wear designs at his Milan headquarters on Thursday, added aubergine, dusty blue and pine green to his range for dresses and tunics as well as clean contrasting combinations like lustrous ivory on black.

The Emporio profile was long and slender in the back for hip-length jackets, coats were cut straight and long, while pants were either loose and swinging wide and straight to the ankle or narrower and ending lower down the leg.
Jacket collars were rounded and fastened high at one side or lying flat with neat lapels, while daytime outfits included suits and trouser suits in pinstripes and Prince of Wales check.

Velvet played a major role, with black devore jackets and tops patterned with small black transparent circular panels or muted silvery and golden prints, or exploited as a military-style stripe down the outside of a grey trouserleg.
"The emphasis is always on the contrast between matt and glossy surfaces," an Emporio statement said.
For evening, ankle length skirts in light fabrics with a simple, sequinned vine motif were worn mischievously with just a sequinned scarf hanging from the models' neck over each breast.
Accessories included floor-length feather boas in greens and blues accompanying a green and blue horizontal striped evening gown, and circular furry stoles worn in a hoop over the elbows.

Contrast and colour also distinguished fashion house Missoni, whose designs were dominated by its bold hallmark wave patterns and irregular vertical and horizontal lines, all coming together in rainbow colour combinations.
Daytime colours were a kaleidoscope of warm sandstone, burnt orange, maroons and browns or bronze, moss and black or, for a more vivid image, reds, purples and rust.

The profile for both day and evening was elongated, with narrow ankle-length shifts and trouserlegs beginning wide immediately at the hip. Shorter skirts were cut in a soft A-line stopping just above the knee.
Coats and jackets were loose-fitting and straight while knits, in the distinctive Missoni stripes, finished on the hip.

For evening, Missoni used the same column-like silhouette for gowns shimmering with the wave and diagonal stripe pattern which came either in glittering blues, greens and purples or in more metallic black, light gold and grey.
Variations for the evening dresses came in the shoulder and neckline, with long sleeves, pencil straps and camisole style bodices, while skirts included an occasional split up one thigh.

Luxury fashion house Gucci pulls the covers off its collection later on Thursday, while top designer Gianfranco Ferre, fashion house Prada, German Jil Sander and design duo Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana all show on Friday.
The shows run through the weekend with top designer Gianni Versace parading his collection on Saturday evening and Armani closing the shows with his top line collection on Sunday.
